blocks.text: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 22/WG 14. (2023, April 1). Programming languages — C (Working draft N3096). https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n3096.pdf

The C working draft was consulted to clarify the domains and results of sqrt and round, finiteness checks, and character classification and conversion. These consultations supplement the <cmath> and <cctype> library interfaces used in C++. Individual lesson notes indicate the sections relevant to each operation.

Köppe, T., Maurer, J., Perchik, D., & Smith, R. (Eds.). (2023, May 10). Working draft, standard for programming language C++ (N4950). ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 22/WG 21. https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2023/n4950.pdf

This C++23 draft supplements the book by clarifying language rules such as evaluation order, return-type deduction, and declarations. It is a technical reference, not the starting point of instruction. Bracketed identifiers, such as [dcl.spec.auto], locate a section without depending on the page numbering of another version.
Primary Source and Consultation of the HTML Draft
Stroustrup, B. (2024). Programming: Principles and practice using C++ (3rd ed.). Addison-Wesley.
Working draft: Programming languages — C++. (n.d.). [HTML edition of the working draft under revision]. Retrieved October 11, 2026, from https://eel.is/c++draft/

The book guides the foundations and progression of the course. Notes in each lesson identify sections that support recalling the concept; explanations, domains, programs, and activities in this path are designed to practice and transfer that knowledge. A reference does not replace justifying a result or checking a program's contract. The HTML C++ draft helps locate the sections cited in lesson notes; it changes as the committee continues its work and is neither an ISO publication nor a fixed C++23 edition. The earlier N4950 document is also retained to distinguish that version's rules from later changes.

A language draft describes its rules; it does not prove that every compiler or environment supports all libraries and functions. In the labs, distinguish a language rule, a program's contract, and the capabilities of the environment running it.
